newsitem.title: CHINA: China's south Hainan pioneers first share aution.
newsitem.headline: China's south Hainan pioneers first share aution.

text.p: China's booming southern Hainan province has pioneered the country's first public auction of institutional shares, officials said on Monday.
The Hainan Materials Auction Market said it had been requested to put up for public auction last Friday a total of six million institutional shares in Hainan Airlines.
The shares were owned by an unidentified local company that needed to pay off debts, an official of the auction house said.
"It was the first time in China, it has been a success," the official said by telephone from the provincial capital, Haikou.
Buyers at the auction paid a total of 4.86 million yuan ($585,542) for 3.8 million of the shares, she said.
The unidentified Hainan firm that had owned the shares was in debt to the amount of five million yuan to the Tongling Investment Co in central Anhui province, she said.
The Tongling Intermediate Court had ordered the Hainan firm to repay debt and authorised the auction house to sell the shares, part of the firm's assets, she said.
After the auction, the new owners would have to apply to securities authorities to transfer ownership, she said.
Institutional shares in China can be traded between institutions -- mostly state-owned entities -- but cannot be publicly listed on its two stock markets.
The airline has listed about 100 million institutional shares on the Beijing-based STAQ system, or the Securities Trade Automatic Quotation system, an official of Hainan Airlines said.
The auctioned shares were part of institutional shares the airline had offered to initial shareholders and had not been listed on the STAQ system, the official said by telephone.
Securities analysts said China has yet to issue rules governing the trading and auction of institutional shares.
Hainan Airlines plans to issue 71 million foreign currency B shares and to list them on the Shanghai stock exchange in the first half of this year, company officials said.
